newsitem.title: USA: Disney buys Pixar stock, sets five film deal.
newsitem.headline: Disney buys Pixar stock, sets five film deal.

text.p: Walt Disney Co. Monday said it forged a new deal with Pixar Animation Studios, its partner in the Academy Award-winning film "Toy Story," and has purchased stock and warrants that could give it a 5 percent stake in the animation company.
Pixar's stock soared more than 27 percent, gaining $3.875 to $18 on Nasdaq in afternoon trading.

Disney said it would produce five movies over the next 10 years with Pixar. The two studios will be equal partners on the five pictures and related products, including home videos, merchandise, interactive- media products and made-for-home-video sequels.

Disney said it will also purchase 1 million shares of Pixar's common stock at $15 a share. In addition, Disney will receive warrants to purchase an additional 1.5 million shares of Pixar common stock at higher prices. If the warrants are exercised, Disney will have a combined total of about 5 percent of Pixar.

Pixar and Disney jointly produced the Academy Award-winning "Toy Story" under their three-picture deal struck in 1991. The remaining pictures from the earlier deal will become the first two pictures under the new deal and will be treated under the new terms.
"We are extremely pleased to again join with Pixar and Steven Jobs in producing future animated features," said Disney Chairman Michael Eisner.

"We are bringing together some of the world's finest creative and technical people to develop what promises to be outstanding, high-quality entertainment. This will be storytelling at its best -- in the 21st century."
Pixar President Jobs said, "...We welcome Disney as a stakeholder in Pixar's future success."

Disney and Pixar said a feature tentatively called "Bugs," directed by Academy Award-winner John Lasseter, will be the first animated picture under the new deal. It is planned for release during the 1998 holiday season.
Released in 1995, the film "Toy Story" was the first full-length feature animation produced entirely by computer.
To date, the film has grossed more than $350 million worldwide, and is projected to sell more than 30 million video cassettes around the world.
Pixar, which has headquarters in Point Richmond, Calif., creates animated feature films and interactive CD-ROM titles.
Disney stock was up 12.5 cents at $75.50 on the New York Stock Exchange.
